description: R1 held-authorization queue (2026-08-17). Retires one open refusal entry by entry_id, setting retired_at exactly once via a predicated update (retired_at IS NULL -> set) — a double-retire is a loud entry_not_found_or_already_retired, never a silent overwrite of an earlier retirement's provenance. Convention (not mechanically enforced): Git-Controller retires an entry once the authorization it waited on is resolved; the owed_by_role holder may also retire directly when the work is abandoned or superseded (retired_reason e.g. 'superseded', 'withdrawn'). Retiring is bookkeeping, never landing permission, which only the register's landing-authorization receipt gives. Accepted entries (record_accepted_authorization) are not retired here: their ids match no refusal row and are refused entry_not_found_or_already_retired; change them with change_accepted_authorization (fire, withdraw, retire). There is no TTL/silent-expiry path anywhere in this queue — every retirement is an explicit, reasoned call.
embedding_description: Closing out a held-authorization refusal entry once the authorization it waited on is resolved, or because the blocked work was superseded or withdrawn. The explicit act that removes a refusal from the open queue — never a timer, never automatic.

result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Routine when it follows a successful commit landing; worth a one-line note otherwise (which entry, why).

error_processor_customizations.action_context: A predicated state update on held_authorization: SET retired_at/retired_reason/retired_by WHERE id = entry_id AND retired_at IS NULL.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: one of entry_id/retired_reason/retired_by/retired_at was empty. entry_not_found_or_already_retired: the predicate matched no row — either entry_id does not exist, names an accepted entry rather than a refusal, or the entry was already retired; the caller cannot need to distinguish these, since either way there is nothing further for this call to do. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: missing_argument means fix the call, do not retry as-is. entry_not_found_or_already_retired after your own prior call is expected and benign (the retire already landed) — confirm via list_held_authorizations rather than treating it as a fault; for an accepted entry use change_accepted_authorization. state_service_unavailable is worth a retry once the platform is up; this verb is safe to retry in general because the predicate makes a repeat call a no-op, not a double-action.
